title: Simplicial compatibility of the slice-cone interpolation prism
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, products and internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and relative joins and right join cones of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]. Let $X$ be any small simplicial set and $c$ a vertex. Define $L=X_{/c}$ by $L_m=\{\tau:\Delta^{m+1}\to X\mid\tau(m+1)=c\}$, with operators extending $\alpha:[l]\to[m]$ by sending the new last vertex to $m+1$. Put $W=L\star\Delta^0$ and $J=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X)\star_X X$, using target evaluation and $1_X$.
For an $n$-simplex $(\epsilon,w)$ of $\Delta^1\times W$, let $\epsilon:[n]\to[1]$ be monotone, and let $r$ be the last base index of the join simplex $w$. If $r\geq0$, its base is represented by $\tau:\Delta^{r+1}\to X$ ending at $c$. Define monotone maps
$$\rho:[1]\times[r]\to[r+1],\qquad \rho(t,j)=\begin{cases}r+1&t=1\text{ and }\epsilon(j)=1,\\
j&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}$$
$$\nu:[n]\to[r+1],\qquad \nu(j)=\begin{cases}j&j\leq r\text{ and }\epsilon(j)=0,\\
r+1&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}$$
Form the relative-join simplex with cut $r$, initial arrow prism $\tau\rho$, target-coordinate simplex $\tau\nu$, and final $X$-block constant at $c$ (omitted when $r=n$). For $r=-1$, use the pure $X$-simplex constant at $c$. These assignments commute with all faces and degeneracies and define a simplicial map $G:\Delta^1\times W\to J$. They are natural in maps of pointed simplicial sets $(X,c)\to(X',c')$. For every base vertex $e:a\to c$ of $L$, the edge $G(-,e)$ is contained in the arrow factor and is represented by the square with horizontal arrows $1_a,e$, source side $1_a$, and target side $e$. On the cone vertex $G$ is constant at the pure $X$-vertex $c$. No horn-filling or quasicategory hypothesis is required.

proof.text: The stated operators make $L$ a simplicial set: if $\widehat\alpha:[l+1]\to[m+1]$ extends $\alpha$ by its new last vertex, then $\widehat{1}=1$ and $\widehat{\alpha\beta}=\widehat\alpha\widehat\beta$, and $\tau\widehat\alpha$ still ends at $c$. The degreewise join formula of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone] gives every $w\in W_n$ a unique cut $-1\leq r\leq n$, a base simplex $\tau$ when $r\geq0$, and the unique final simplex of $\Delta^0$. Under $\alpha:[l]\to[n]$ its new base block is the initial segment $\alpha^{-1}\{0,\ldots,r\}$.

proof.text: The identities of step 4 show equality of all coordinates after restriction. The initial arrow simplex becomes $\tau\rho(1\times\beta)=\tau'\rho'$, and the full target coordinate becomes $\tau\nu\alpha=\tau'\nu'$. The final block remains constant at $c$, with the unique empty-block value when necessary, and its cut parameter is $b_r\alpha=b_{r'}$. By the degreewise operator of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join], these are exactly the coordinates of $\alpha^*G_n(\epsilon,w)$, so they equal $G_l(\epsilon\alpha,\alpha^*w)$. This includes $r=n$, $r'=l$, repeated values of $\alpha$, and omitted vertices.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, final construction of gamma-minus: rho and rho-prime. Explicit degreewise extension over the right cone and operator checks supplied here.

proof.text: If $r\geq0$ but the inverse-image base block is empty, every $\alpha(k)>r$, so $\nu\alpha$ is constant at $r+1$. Restriction deletes the entire arrow block and leaves the pure $X$-simplex $c_l$, including its constant target coordinate. This equals the rule for the new cut $r'=-1$. If already $r=-1$, restriction of a constant simplex is constant. Thus the operator equality holds for every monotone $\alpha$, including those deleting either whole join block. Together with step 5 it proves all face and degeneracy equations and defines the asserted simplicial map $G$.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, final construction of gamma-minus: rho and rho-prime. Explicit degreewise extension over the right cone and operator checks supplied here.

proof.text: For a pointed simplicial map $h:(X,c)\to(X',c')$, the slice map takes $\tau$ to $h\tau$, preserving the cut, and the induced arrow map is postcomposition by $h$. Therefore the initial prism becomes $(h\tau)\rho=h(\tau\rho)$, the target coordinate becomes $(h\tau)\nu=h(\tau\nu)$, and the final constant block becomes constant at $c'$. The induced relative-join map has exactly these coordinates by [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]. The pure-factor case is also preserved, proving naturality in all degrees.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, final construction of gamma-minus: rho and rho-prime. Explicit degreewise extension over the right cone and operator checks supplied here.

proof.text: For a base vertex $e:a\to c$, restrict to $\Delta^1\times\{e\}$. All its join cuts are pure initial cuts, so its image lies in the arrow factor. To compute its nondegenerate edge, take $n=r=1$, $\epsilon(j)=j$, and let $\tau$ be the degeneracy of $e$ given by $[2]\to[1]$, $0,1\mapsto0$ and $2\mapsto1$. The arrow prism has value $a$ at $(0,0),(1,0),(0,1)$ and $c$ at $(1,1)$; as a simplicial map it is $e$ precomposed with the monotone map $(t,j)\mapsto1$ exactly when $t=j=1$. At homotopy time $j=0$ its arrow is $1_a$; at $j=1$ it is $e$. Its source side $t=0$ is $1_a$ and its target side $t=1$ is $e$. This specifies the requested square, including its simplices, rather than just its vertices.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, final construction of gamma-minus: rho and rho-prime. Explicit degreewise extension over the right cone and operator checks supplied here.

proof.text: On $\Delta^1$ times the cone vertex every $w$ is pure final, so $r=-1$ in every degree. The rule is independent of $\epsilon$ and always gives $i_X(c_n)$, the constant simplicial map at the pure $X$-vertex $c$. Every construction above used only precomposition, the explicit ordinal formulas, and degreewise joins and pullbacks; hence it applies to every pointed small simplicial set without any horn-filling hypothesis.
